Byomkesh.description: The protagonist, a sharp and observant detective known as a 'truth-seeker' (satyanweshi), who solves mysteries with logical reasoning.

Ajit.description: Byomkesh's close friend and chronicler, who narrates their adventures and assists in investigations.

Satyabati.description: Ajit's wife, known for her wit and strong opinions; she often participates in household discussions.

Shrichintamani Kundu.description: An elderly, paralyzed landlord who seeks Byomkesh's help after being implicated in a murder case involving his tenant.

Ramadhin.description: Chintamani Kundu's loyal Hindustani servant who assists with household tasks.

Tapan Sen.description: Supposedly a young man who rents a house from Chintamani Kundu, later revealed to be an alias of Promila Pal.

Shanta.description: Presented as Tapan Sen's wife, later revealed to be the same person as Tapan Sen, actually Promila Pal in disguise.

Bijoy Bhaduri.description: A senior police inspector, diligent and suspicious by nature, involved in the murder investigation.

Bidhubhushan Aich.description: A Burdwan police employee who is murdered in front of the twin houses.

Promila Pal.description: The true identity of Tapan Sen/Shanta, a fugitive and murderer who disguises herself as both man and woman.

Nengti Dutta.description: A precocious and cheeky youth who befriends Byomkesh and is fascinated by detective work.

Byomkesh Samagra.description: The title of the complete collection of Byomkesh Bakshi stories.

Bankimchandra.description: Refers to Bankimchandra Chattopadhyay, a renowned Bengali novelist and author of 'Devi Chowdhurani'.

Devi Chowdhurani.description: A famous novel by Bankimchandra Chattopadhyay featuring a female bandit leader.

zenana ward.description: A section of a jail reserved for female prisoners.

Burdwan.description: A district in West Bengal, referenced here as the origin of the murdered police employee and the jail.

Calcutta.description: Now known as Kolkata, the capital city of West Bengal and the main setting of the story.

Chetla.description: A neighborhood in southeastern Calcutta, mentioned as the location of the girls' school.

Madrasi.description: A term used to refer to people from the southern Indian region of Madras (now Chennai).

Hindustani.description: Refers to people or things associated with northern India or the Hindi-speaking region.

Khotta.description: A term referring to a community or group, often of North Indian Muslim origin, used here for a servant.

Jemadar.description: A police or military rank in India, typically denoting a junior officer or sergeant.

Ardhanarishvara.description: A composite form of the Hindu god Shiva and goddess Parvati, symbolizing the synthesis of masculine and feminine energies.

Magnamainak.description: Appears as a heading or section title, possibly a reference to a mythological or literary figure.

boti.description: A traditional Bengali curved blade used for cutting vegetables, often operated with the foot.

para.description: A Bengali term for a neighborhood or locality.

taktaposh.description: A wooden cot or daybed commonly found in Bengali households.

attaché case.description: A small, flat suitcase used for carrying documents, popular in urban India.

mashima.description: A Bengali term meaning 'aunt', used for an elder woman.

mesomoshai.description: A Bengali term for 'uncle', specifically mother's sister's husband.

mem.description: A colloquial term derived from 'madam', used in India to refer to European or Anglo-Indian women.
